en: The commencement of the fifth canto in the glorious Ānandarāmāyaṇa, contained within the illustrious Śatakoṭirāmacarita.
Viṣṇudāsa said:
O Guru, please reveal to me that consecration of the kuśa grass which was proclaimed in the Śrī Rāmarakṣā and performed by that very sage.
Having heard these words of the disciple— "Please recite the excellent and meritorious Rāmarakṣā, which brings peace to children"— Rāmadāsa spoke these words.
Śrī Rāmadāsa said:
You have asked well, O disciple; the Rāma-rakṣā is now being told, which was previously spoken by Śambhu to Girijā for the sake of Skanda.
The illustrious Śiva said: "O Goddess, today consecrate the Rāmarakṣā for Skanda’s son, the slayer of Tāraka; he shall become capable."
Having spoken thus, Śiva recited the Rāma-rakṣā to the woman;
[he who is] saluted by those who have purified themselves and conquered their senses, [recites] Rāmacandra.
Now, the meditation:

[One should visualize the deity] eternally holding in his left lotus-hand the staff of a bow, and in his right hand a single arrow; and behind him, he constantly bears his beloved [consort] along with the weight of a quiver.

I worship the dark-complexioned Rāma, who is skilled at dispelling the mental anguish of those who bow before him, and whose body is joined with Jānakī and Lakṣmaṇa as they dwell on his left and right sides.
Oṃ. Of this Śrī Rāmarakṣā Stotra-mantra, Budha Kauśika is the seer (ṛṣi);
the venerable Rāmacandra is the deity (devatā); "Rāma" is the seed-syllable (bīja);
Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandaḥ); its application (viniyoga) is for the purpose of recitation for the pleasure of the venerable Rāma.
Oṃ.
The life-story of Raghunātha extends for hundreds of millions of verses;
yet every single syllable destroys the great sins of men.
Having meditated upon Rāma, who is dark-complexioned like a blue lotus, with eyes like lotuses, accompanied by Jānakī and Lakṣmaṇa, and adorned with a crown of matted locks; || 8 ||
Having seen the unborn, all-pervading Lord, the destroyer of night-stalkers, who had manifested with ease to protect the world, holding in his hand a bow and arrows along with a sword.
The wise person should recite the Rāmarakṣā, which destroys sin and grants all desires:
"May Rāghava protect my head; may the son of Daśaratha protect my forehead. (10)
May the son of Kausalyā protect my two eyes; may he who is dear to Viśvāmitra protect my ears;
may the protector of sacrifices protect my nose; and may he who is affectionate toward the son of Sumitrā protect my mouth. 11.
May the Lord who is the storehouse of all arts protect my tongue; may he who is praised by Bharata protect my throat;
may he who wields divine weapons protect my shoulders; and may he who broke the bow of Śiva protect my arms. || 12 ||
May the Lord of Sītā protect my two hands; may the conqueror of Paraśurāma protect my heart; may the best of the Raghus protect my sides; and may the delighter of the Ikṣvākus protect my two flanks.
May the destroyer of Khara protect my waist; may he who has Jāmbavān as his refuge protect my navel; may the lord of Sugrīva protect my hips; and may the master of Hanumān protect my thighs.
May the best of the Raghus protect my thighs; may the destroyer of the race of Rākṣasas protect my private parts;
may the builder of the bridge protect my knees; and may the slayer of the ten-faced one protect my shanks. || 15 ||
May Rāma, who bestows the glory of Vibhīṣaṇa, protect his feet; may he protect his entire body.
Whatever virtuous person recites this protection endowed with the power of Rāma, [for him there shall be well-being].
He shall be long-lived, happy, possessed of sons, victorious, and disciplined. || 16 ||
Those who roam the netherworld, the earth, and the sky, moving by means of deception, are not even able to look upon one protected by the names of Rāma. 17.
Remembering "Rāma," "Rāmabhadra," or "Rāmacandra," a person is not tainted by sins and attains both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
The entire world is protected by the single mantra of Rāma’s name;
for him who wears it around his neck, all spiritual perfections (siddhis) are held in the palm of his hand.
Whoever recites this armor of Rāma, known by the name Vajrapañjara, shall have his commands unimpeded everywhere and obtain victory and auspiciousness. || 20 ||
Just as Hara had instructed him in a dream regarding this Rāmarakṣā,
so did the wise Kauśika write it down in the morning upon waking.
The heroic Rāma, son of Daśaratha, is mighty and has Lakṣmaṇa as his follower.
The descendant of Kakutstha, the perfect Supreme Person, who increases the joy of Kausalyā.
The piercer of the Vedānta, the Lord of Sacrifice, the Ancient Supreme Person, the Beloved of Jānakī, the Glorious One of immeasurable prowess. || 23 ||
Whoever, devoted and endowed with faith, should constantly recite these [mantras], obtains merit greater than that of a horse-sacrifice; of this there is no doubt. (24)
May Rāma, our desire incarnate, who goes forth armored, wearing a breastplate and a sword, bearing arrows and a bow, and accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, protect us. 25.
Young, endowed with beauty, delicate yet possessed of great strength,
with eyes as broad as lotuses, they were clothed in bark and black antelope skins.
Subsisting on fruits and roots, self-controlled, ascetics, and observers of celibacy—
these two brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, are the sons of Daśaratha.
Those two renowned archers, Rama and Lakshmana, who carry swords at their sides and wear the side-locks of youth, may both of them protect me on the road. (28)
May the two best of the Raghus—the refuge of all beings and the most excellent among all archers, the destroyers of the race of Rākṣasas—protect us. (29)
May Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, with their bows strung and ready, their arrows smeared with poison, and their quivers fastened to their chests, always go before me on the path for my protection. (30)
He is the grove of wish-fulfilling trees, the cessation of all suffering, the delight of the three worlds; may that glorious Lord Rāma be our refuge. 31.
Salutations to Rāma, to Rāmabhadra, to Rāmacandra, to the Creator, to the Lord of the Raghus, to the Protector, and to the husband of Sītā. || 32 ||
Śrī Rāma, joy of the Raghus, Rāma, Rāma;
Śrī Rāma, elder brother of Bharata, Rāma, Rāma;
Śrī Rāma, fierce in battle, Rāma, Rāma.
O Śrī Rāma, take refuge; Rāma, Rāma! || 33 ||

I take refuge in that Śrī Rāmacandra, who delights the world, who is steadfast on the field of battle, whose eyes are like lotuses, the lord of the Raghu dynasty, the embodiment of compassion, and the mine of mercy. || 34 ||
I bow to that joy of the Raghus, who has Lakṣmaṇa at his right and the daughter of Janaka at his left, with Māruti in front of him;
he who turned the lord of the waters into a mere puddle for cattle and reduced the Rākṣasa to the size of a mosquito.
I salute the son of the Wind-god, a jewel within the great garland of the Rāmāyaṇa. || 36 ||
O heap of sins, stay far away; O diseases, remain at a distance.
The wielder of the bow, Rāma, ever dwells within our hearts. 37.

I take refuge in the son of the Wind, the foremost among the wise, whose speed is as swift as thought and equal to the force of the wind, who has conquered his senses, the leader of the host of monkeys, and the messenger of the illustrious Rāma. 38.

O Rāma, O Rāma, for the sake of liberation from the bonds of worldly existence, I meditate upon your lotus feet, which are always saluted by the crowns of the lords of gods and men, and constantly contemplated in the minds of yogis. (37)
Rāma, the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa, the best of the Raghus, the husband of Sītā, the handsome one;
the descendant of Kakutstha, an ocean of compassion, a treasure-house of virtues, dear to the Brahmins, and righteous;
the king of kings, true to his promise, the son of Daśaratha, the dark-complexioned one, the very embodiment of peace.
I bow to Rāghava, the enemy of Rāvaṇa, the ornament of the Raghu dynasty, who delights the world. 40.
Whoever, having risen in the morning, recites these names of Rāma, one who is childless obtains a son, and one who seeks wealth obtains wealth. (41)
Rama is my mother; Ramachandra is my father; Ramachandra is my lord; Ramachandra is my friend.
Ramachandra, the compassionate one, is my all-in-all; I know no other, I truly know no other, I know no other.

If the life-giving seed-mantra of the nectar of Śrī Rāma’s name has entered the mind, then for those entering even the halāhala poison, the fire of universal destruction, or the mouth of death, whence can there be fear? (43)

The name of Raghunātha, preceded by the word *śrī*, with the word *jaya* in the middle, and again employed at the end—by chanting this twenty-one times, one destroys the sin of killing ten million Brahmins. (44)
Thus has this Rāmarakṣā been declared by me to you, O Daughter of the Lord of Mountains;
it is that which was previously taught by me to Viśvāmitra in a dream.
Rāmadāsa said: Having heard what was thus instructed by Śiva, the goddess, daughter of the mountain king,
recited the Rāmarakṣā and consecrated Skanda with mantras.
By her very power and strength, the six-faced one slew the demon Tāraka; in an instant, he became one who had accomplished his purpose in the past.
This very Rāmarakṣā, which bestows great merit, has been recounted by me to you;
by the mere hearing of it, no one shall have any fear. (48)
This unprecedented consecration of Kuśa and Lava by Vālmīki has been performed;
it was taught by me for the purpose of pacifying the seizing spirits of children. (49)
For the sake of pacifying the planetary influences of children, this most excellent Rāmarakṣā, which wards off the flood of great evils, should be recited continuously. (50)
There is no hymn superior to this; there is no recitation superior to this;
there is nothing whatsoever superior to this—I speak the truth, the absolute truth. (51)
Thus ends the fifth canto, titled "The Narration of the Rāmarakṣā," in the Janmakāṇḍa of the glorious Ānandarāmāyaṇa of Vālmīki, which is contained within the illustrious Śatakoṭi Rāmacarita.
